intro.title: Move Zeroes (2-pointer version)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that moves all zeros in an array to the end while keeping the order of non-zero elements unchanged. You'll learn the two-pointer technique, a core algorithm pattern that uses two indices to traverse and rearrange elements efficiently. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays, loops, and conditional logic. This beginner-friendly approach will help you understand how to solve array manipulation problems with optimal performance.
intro.usecase: The two-pointer technique for moving zeroes mirrors how real applications handle data filtering and organization. In e-commerce dashboards, administrators use similar logic to push out-of-stock items to the end while keeping available products visible. Content management systems apply this pattern when users want to temporarily hide certain entries without deleting them, maintaining the active items at the front. This approach is also used in data visualization tools where zero-value data points need to be grouped separately from meaningful metrics. Developers encounter this pattern whenever they need to reorganize arrays while preserving relative order of non-target elements.
